findings.title: Public findMany method removed and return types changed without updating callers
findings.body: The `findMany` method was removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions`, and `getAuthorizationConditions`/`getFilterConditions` now return `Prisma.Sql` instead of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput`. The constructor's `options` type was also widened. Any consumer that called `service.findMany(...)` or consumed the object-shaped conditions will fail to compile or silently change behavior. Neither the diff nor the PR description shows updated callers, so the PR cannot be merged safely without auditing usages across the repo.

findings.title: Caching tests deleted without replacement
findings.body: The entire `describe("Caching")` block (tests 'should cache authorization conditions' and 'should cache filter conditions') was removed in this PR. The service still caches `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions` and that behavior is not tested anywhere now. The PR description does not mention removing these tests.

findings.title: Final test no longer exercises the service's findMany path and runs against an unverified table
findings.body: The former `findMany` integration test, which exercised the real service entry point, was replaced with a hand-written `$queryRaw` that selects from "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" using the conditions. This test no longer verifies anything the service itself returns, and it depends on the denormalized table/view being populated for the inserted booking (the booking is created directly in Booking, so the denormalized row must be produced by a trigger or sync). If that sync is absent in the test DB the assertion `toEqual([{id}])` fails, and if it is present the test silently depends on it. The test should document or set up that dependency.

findings.title: Array-ordering assertions depend on unspecified query order
findings.body: The org scope test expects `teamId = ANY` and `userId = ANY` arrays in a specific order (org, team, team2, team3). Those arrays come from `findAllByParentId` and `findAllByTeamIds`, which have no ORDER BY guarantee, so `toEqual` on the Prisma.Sql values can fail nondeterministically. Sorting before comparison or using an order-insensitive matcher would make the test stable.
